rites.name: Rillaurnia
rites.text: Rillaurnia is a concept of the Courts in Silanneth, the idea of a bound oath that lets a ruling council hold a door open between worlds. It was first named during the Age of Sundering, when landfall broke older covenants and the councils had to rebuild them.

rites.name: Thyustis
rites.text: Thyustis is a concept of the Arcane Realm, a binding that gave shape to the Pact sworn during the Fall of Silanneth, when worlds broke apart into Shards. It belongs to the early Age of the first sovereign, a time of groves and growing kingdoms whose roots held the broken lands together.

rites.name: Osavseth
rites.text: Osavseth is the concept of a binding oath, the living thread that held the broken worlds of Silanneth together during the Sundering. In the Age of the first sovereign its meaning became the foundation of the groves and growing kingdoms that followed.

rites.name: Zephavsora
rites.text: Zephavsora is a concept of the Arcane Realm of Silanneth, the force of sworn promises that held the Pact together after worlds broke in the Sundering. It was bound into the groves and growing kingdoms of the first sovereign's age, shaping the boundaries that kept the Shards from drifting apart.

rites.name: Syivsora
rites.text: Syivsora is the concept of a binding oath that holds fragments of a broken sky together, carried through the Holy Age as a rule of flame and temple. In the Fall it was the first word spoken when worlds split, and the orders that followed still measure their vows by its weight.

rites.name: Drarkok
rites.text: Drarkok is a concept of Silanneth's Arcane Realm, personified as the ember-thread that bound the shattered worlds during the Fall and the Sundering. Its Holy Age orders held that its flame could be borrowed but never owned, and the Pact was sworn in its name.

rites.name: Thouzhun
rites.text: Thouzhun is the concept of the wall that holds a grove against the wild, binding the first sovereign's boundaries into a single lasting promise. In the Walled Age it was spoken into stone and oath, so that a kingdom's edges would stay where they were drawn.

rites.name: Osiasora
rites.text: Osiasora is a concept of the Walled Age in Silanneth, a principle of holding walls and sworn orders that bound the wild groves. Its chief expression is the ward-binding, a sustained working that keeps old boundaries standing through the first sovereign's reign.

rites.name: Ilyinnemora
rites.text: Ilyinnemora is a concept of the Arcane realm in the Silanneth omniverse, a discipline of patient scholarship that lets its practitioners read the traces of old serpentine sovereigns in stone and soil. Those who master it can recognise, at a glance, any hall, nest, or hoard that once answered to a wyrm. Its earliest records in the sixth era were kept by tutors who taught apprentices to memorise ash-marks and scale-polished thresholds.

rites.name: Ryimeirwen
rites.text: Ryimeirwen is the concept of a branching ending, a single thought in Silanneth that the Library files among its many possible futures during the age of the first sovereign. It is said to shape how groves and growing kingdoms imagine their own endings, though it has no body of its own.

rites.name: Vesithora
rites.text: Vesithora is the concept of a branching future, held in Silanneth's Arcane Realm during the Age of the first sovereign, when groves were still growing into kingdoms. Its authority is the shelving of every possible outcome, so that each ending waits within the Library until the choosing hand reaches for it.

rites.name: Anasamlaala
rites.text: Anasamlaala is a concept born in the Arcane Realm of Silanneth, pictured as a branching thread that the Library files among the many endings of the Three Futures. In the Age of the first sovereign, when groves were still turning into kingdoms, it was said to tilt which outcome a seed would follow.
